title.narrative: Hurricane Beryll Child Centered Response Project

description.narrative: Hurricane Beryll moved across the South Coast of Jamaica mostly affecting the parishes of Westmoreland, St Elizabeth, Manchester, Clarendon, St Catherine, and Trelawny. It is estimated that approximately 160,000 persons are in need. UNICEF has targeted 37,000 children in need from the affected areas. Preliminary results indicate that in the affected communities there is urgent response needed in the areas of WASH, shelter, food and support to livelihood activities. Through this project women and children will be assisted with the provision of water for drinking, cooking, personal and domestic hygiene, and other minimum sanitation and hygiene standards and menstrual hygiene. Through this intervention mothers, fathers, and caregivers will be provided with support needed to ensure infant feeding meets the standards so that the emergence of acute malnutrition does not worsen the impact. The project will also allow families with children in poverty to access food and other essential goods through cash transfers or vouchers for immediate use. The project will also support vector control measures in the affected areas to prevent the spread of water borne illness that may have a severe impact on children. Finally, programmes to support children psychosocial support, SEA reporting mechanism, and the generation of VAC/GBV prevention awareness will be implemented. The project will be completed within a 6 month period through UNICEF staff, implementing partners and consultancies. The relevant monitoring and evaluation activities will be put in place to ensure that the project activities are carried out appropriately.
